title1: Pilot Project No. 24: Separation monies — w/c 2493 to w/c2572
title2: Pilot Project No. 24: Separation monies — w/c 2493 to w/c2572
text: A temporary measure under Pilot Project No. 24 applies to separation monies paid due to a separation from employment on claims with a BPC or allocation start date between March 30, 2025 (w/c 2493) and October 10 , 2026 (w/c 2572 ). When separation monies are paid for that period, they are not allocated. Separation monies that are not allocated cannot extend a benefit period (BP). This measure applies to all benefit types (BTs) for initial, renewal and continuing claims. This measure applies to the following monies when paid due to separation: vacation pay pay in lieu of notice severance pay retirement allowance and retirement leave credits sick leave credits closure bonus separation and retirement bonus settlement payments To be considered under the temporary measures, one of the following conditions must be met: the BPC is between March 30, 2025 (w/c 2493), and October 10 , 2026 (w/c 2572 ); the separation monies would otherwise be allocated under EIR 36(9) to 36(11) and the first week of allocation falls within the period beginning March 30, 2025 (w/c 2493) to October 10 , 2026 (w/c 2572 ). EIR 36(9) 36(11) If neither condition is met, the officer allocates the separation monies using the usual Earnings procedures. For more information, including examples, the officer refers to BE Memo BE-2025-05 . Earnings BE Memo BE-2025-05

title1: Changing the type of parental benefits
title2: Changing the type of parental benefits
text: Clients can change the type of parental benefits requested if the request is made before any parental benefits have been paid to any parent. Once at least one week of parental benefits has been paid to any parent (even as little as $1), the type of parental benefits that was selected by the first parent who applied cannot be changed . If any other parent is paid a different type of parental benefits than the type selected by the first parent who applied, the benefit type (BT) on the other parents’ claims is converted to the BT selected by the first parent. If a request to change the type of parental benefits is submitted before benefits have been paid, although benefits are subsequently paid as a result of processing delays or automated payments, the request may still be granted.

title1: Extending the benefit period (BP) and parental window (PW)
title2: Extending the benefit period (BP) and parental window (PW)
text: Hospitalization of the child for whom parental benefits are being claimed is grounds to extend the BP and PW. The BP and PW can also be extended for personnel of the Canadian military who are unable to collect their parental benefits because of an imperative military requirement. For more information, the officer refers to Extension of the benefit period . Extension of the benefit period The PW is also extended when a client entitled to parental benefits is entitled to a BP extension for special benefits. When this occurs, the BP and PW are both extended. For more information, the officer refers to Benefit period: Extension for special benefits — Table . A Parental Client Record is created for every client requesting parental benefits. The Parental Client Record consists of the client’s SIN, the arrival or placement week (APW) and the other parent’s SIN, if it has been provided. Once a claim is finalized, the system links Parental Client Records for all clients who are sharing parental benefits for the same child. The Parental sharing validation process creates a Claim Review (CR) Parental Benefits Validation WI when one of the following conditions is met: The parental benefit type on all linked Parental Client Records is not the same. The total number of parental weeks requested on all linked Parental Client Records exceeds the maximum number of shareable parental benefit weeks. Updating the Parental Client Record The officer inputs the other parent’s SIN using the Parental Benefits Validation transaction in the Enquiry menu in FTS. This screen also displays linked parents’ SINs and the associated APW. Note Note
